To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) object-based concepts can provide a designer with the means to control interference, (2) interference can be limited in a class of systems, (3) a transformational style can be used to develop systems in this class, and (4) this transformational style can introduce concurrency only in the final stage of design.

(a) the object graph of an object-based design model can be used to constrain inference in the design model; and that (b) the object graph can be used to control the order of introduction of concurrency into the design model.
(i) object graphs are an appropriate model for concurrent programs, and (ii) the object graph model is a suitable basis for a development method for concurrent systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a compositional method for the development of object-oriented concurrent programs, in which the programmer can control interference.
finding a way to use object-based language features to provide the designer with control over the amount of interference that is present in a concurrent system.
developing methods for the design and development of concurrent programs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper shows how to constrain inference in an object-based model of concurrent systems.
the object graph is a powerful tool for limiting interference, and that the transformational style of design is an appropriate one for systems with limited interference.
this paper provides a basis for a method of design which is compositional, in the sense that a design can be decomposed into a number of smaller designs, each of which can be developed independently.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a design method for concurrent systems in which interference is controlled and which can be used to produce a transformational style development method.
we are exploring ways in which the object-based language concepts can be exploited to provide an object-oriented development method for concurrent systems.
we are exploring the use of object-based language concepts as a basis for compositional development methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of object-based concepts can help to reduce interference in concurrent systems.
object-based concepts can provide a designer with an intuitive way of controlling interference.
interference can be controlled by using object-based language concepts to constrain inference.
